newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads flat, investors skittish.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads flat, investors skittish.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were unchanged in thin trade on Monday as uncertainty over Federal Reserve monetary policy kept investors at bay, while high-yields ended mixed, dealers said.

Talk of a possible tightening of short-term interest rates at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting March 25 pushed investors to the sidelines, traders said, leaving only the most liquid issues as fodder for activity.
"Accounts are really confused as to what the next step is going to be and that doesn't bode well for the week with the Fed not meeting until next Tuesday," one trader said.

The trader added that spreads, while wider over the past week, have yet to widen enough to attract the attention of total return investors. Monday's lack of volume kept spreads at Friday's levels, he said.

Dealers stressed skittish sentiments washed over from U.S. Treasuries, which ended lower following signs of strength in the housing sector and hawkish comments from San Francisco Fed president Robert Parry.
The benchmark 30-year closed down 5/32 to yield 6.96 percent after touching the psychologically important seven percent level near mid-session.

Back in high-yields, the 11-3/8 percent senior subordinated notes of Flagstar Cos Inc were flat at 35 bid throughout the session despite speculation the company would miss a $7 million interest payment.
One analyst late in the session said the payment was indeed missed, although the company would not issue a confirmation.

Other market sources said Flagstar made its interest payment on its 10-3/4 percent senior notes, however. The notes were quoted up one point to 97 for most of the session before closing above 98, traders said.

Elsewhere, Hyperion Telecommunications Inc on Monday said it entered into an agreement with MCI Communications Corp that names it as a preferred provider for new and end user dedicated access circuits.
In return, MCI would be issued warrants to purchase 2.5 percent of Hyperion stock.
Hyperion debt gained 1/2 point on the news, a trader said.

Other high-yield issues were flat to marginally lower in thin trade, dealers said. Few accounts were committed to trades and were said to play the market more defensive despite still-strong cash positions.

"Its been a slow day today and there's a lot of mixed stuff," one trader said. "There are markets out there but they're wide and it just seems like no one wants to do anything because there is uncertainty about the direction."
The market was also focused on up to $2 billion in fresh high-yield supply, players said.
No new issues were priced on Monday.
